title: A Pacific temperature contrast cut six-month volume forecast error by 16.39% with seasonal state slopes at 2000-2023 origins
abstract: We tested whether an east-west Pacific temperature contrast adds six-month warm water volume forecast information when current temperature and volume slopes change with season. We used fixed NOAA GODAS and CPC ERSSTv5 records. At 288 monthly origins in 2000-2023, adding current and six-month past Nino 3 minus Nino 4 anomalies reduced mean squared error by 16.39%. RMSE fell from 0.81123 to 0.74178 in units of 10^14 cubic metres. The conditional 95% three-year block interval for error reduction was 3.94% to 27.08%. The one-year block interval included zero, as did the 2012-2023 interval. Planned alternate seasonal models retained positive three-year block limits. Thus, these smooth seasonal state effects did not remove the gain against the specified baseline. This extends a campaign result on the same data; it is not independent confirmation. Revised records, few cycles, model choice, release timing and conditional uncertainty limit inference. No physical cause or operational skill is established. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, score and numerical checks, and a figure.
